newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Bolger still rates his chances of govt even.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Bolger still rates his chances of govt even.

text.p: National Party caretaker Prime Minister Jim Bolger on Thursday said the pace of coalition talks was quickening, but he still thought the chances of a conservative National-led government emerging from the talks was an even bet.

"The pace is certainly quickening, the parliament is going to open very soon and everybody knows it is very desirable to have the issue resolved before that," Bolger said as he went into another round of talks with nationalist New Zealand First.
Asked how optimistic he was Bolger said: "I think we are still 50-50 --- that has always been my position."

Nationalist NZ First holds the balance of power after the October 12 election and is negotiating separately with both the conservative incumbent National and centre-left Labour over the shape of the next government.
"We have still got quite a lot of work to do," Bolger said, but declined to name the day pariament would sit.
Parliament must meet no later than December 13, but the outgoing government tentatively set December 10 as the first sitting day.
Bolger said December 10 was an option but it did not have to be that day.
Going into the talks with National, NZ First leader Winston Peters reiterated he was leaving negotiations over the support of the left-wing Alliance for a centre-left government to Labour.
Labour held talks for two hours with the Alliance on Wednesday and plans further talks today after the Alliance caucus meets. Labour has briefed NZ First on the talks.
If NZ First opts to back National the two would command 61 votes in the 120 seat single chamber parliament.
But NZ First and Labour would have only 54 seats and would need the backing of the 13 Alliance MPs on crucial votes of confidence and money supply.
